properties.areaDesc: Coastal waters from Cameron LA to High Island TX out 20 NM; Coastal waters from Intracoastal City to Cameron LA out 20 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 9 at 8:56AM CDT until September 9 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
SMWLCH

The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Cameron LA to High Island TX out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Intracoastal City to Cameron LA out 20 NM...

* Until 1000 AM CDT.

* At 855 AM CDT, a cluster of storms producing waterspouts was
located near West Cameron 45, or 14 nm southwest of Cameron,
moving west at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Off duty forecaster.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
West Cameron 66, West Cameron 45, West Cameron 53, West Cameron 65,
West Cameron 62, West Cameron 73, West Cameron 48, and Cameron.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.description:

showers through this afternoon that may lead to flooding.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The Big Island.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed
due to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may
receive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid
runoff.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

showers through this afternoon that may lead to flooding.
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 9 at 4:24AM PDT until September 10 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot late-season conditions expected with high
temperatures up to 112 to 116 in Death Valley and the Colorado
River Valley; up to 105 to 110 in the Las Vegas Valley, Moapa
Valley, and Pahrump Valley.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada.

* WHEN...From 10 AM PDT /10 AM MST/ to 8 PM PDT /8 PM MST/ Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and
loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 9 at 4:22AM MST until September 11 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot and humid conditions. Afternoon temperatures
108 to 114 expected. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Imperial County Southwest, Imperial County West, and
Imperial Valley.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued September 9 at 3:21AM CDT until September 10 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH IN EFFECT FROM THURSDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH EARLY
THURSDAY EVENING DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR SOUTHWEST
AND PORTIONS OF NORTHWEST NORTH DAKOTA...

.Warm and breezy conditions are expected over western North Dakota on
Thursday ahead of an approaching cold front. Temperatures are
forecast to climb into the upper 80s, with afternoon humidities of 12
to 20 percent. Winds on Thursday afternoon are forecast to be
westerly 15 to 25 mph with gusts to 35 mph. Due to the low humidity
and breezy conditions with abundant dry vegetation, critical fire
weather conditions are forecast to occur Thursday afternoon into
early Thursday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of northwest and southwest North Dakota.

* TIMING...From Thursday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* WINDS...West winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity from 12 and 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions are
forecast to occur. Listen for later forecast updates and a possible
upgrade of this watch to a Red Flag Warning.

NWSheadline: FIRE WEATHER WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM THURSDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH THURSDAY EVENING

properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 419, 420, 421, 422, 425, and
427.

* WIND...Westerly 15 to 30 MPH with occasional gusts up to 40
MPH. The strongest winds will occur Thursday afternoon.

* HUMIDITY...10 to 15% Wednesday afternoon and as low as 5%
Thursday afternoon. Poor overnight recoveries Wednesday night,
as low as 20% to 30%.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

* WHAT...Temperatures of 88 to 108 expected.

* WHERE...Calabasas and Agoura Hills, Eastern San Fernando Valley,
Eastern Santa Monica Mountains Recreational Area, Los Angeles
County Beaches, Los Angeles County Inland Coast including Downtown
Los Angeles, Los Angeles County San Gabriel Valley, Malibu Coast,
Palos Verdes Hills, Western San Fernando Valley, and Western Santa
Monica Mountains Recreational Area

* WHEN...From 8 AM this morning to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Humid conditions will add to heat discomfort.
Heat peaking on Wednesday for most areas, except likely peaking
Thursday for the Santa Barbara South Coast.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 9 at 2:08AM MDT until September 10 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Riverton has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from noon today to 9 PM MDT Thursday.
the Fire Weather Watch is no longer in effect.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In Southwest WY Fire Zones...277...279.
In West Central WY Fire Zone....278.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In Southwest WY...Sweetwater...Uinta.
In West Central WY...Lincoln...Sublette.

* IMPACTS: Low Humidities and Strong Gusty Winds could cause
erratic fire behavior.

* WIND: West 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 25 mph. Thursday, west 15
to 25 mph with gusts of 30 to 35 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 10 percent. RH recovery will be fair to poor
tonight in zones 277 and 279.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 8 at 10:05PM CDT until September 9 at 8:20PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas near
the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 26.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 PM CDT Tuesday was 26.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 18.8 feet Sunday
evening.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 26.2
feet on 03/19/1995.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.
